description: A tenant-isolated document API with an external identity provider.

notes: Illustrative fixture, not an actual system assessment.
All six STRIDE categories considered; only the illustrative session threat is retained.

threats.scenario: A stolen session could be replayed.

observations.summary: Identity is an external trust dependency.

assumptions: Description-only illustrative input, not a production assessment.
dfd:
flowchart LR
  user["User"] -->|Document request| api
  subgraph app["Application trust boundary"]
    api["API"]
  end
  api -->|Validate identity| idp["External IdP"]
  idp -->|Identity assertion| api
attack_tree:
flowchart TD
  goal["Impersonate a user"] --> both["AND"]
  both --> stolen["Assumption: attacker obtains session"]
  both --> replay["STRIDE-001: session accepted on replay"]

mitigations.text: API: revoke compromised sessions and enforce bounded session lifetimes. Verify revoked and expired sessions are rejected at every protected route. Session theft before revocation remains a residual risk; actual session controls need confirmation.

damage.rationale: Confidential document access is serious, assuming a compromised user can read sensitive files.

reproducibility.rationale: Replay could be repeatable while a stolen session remains valid; actual defenses are unspecified.

exploitability.rationale: Obtaining a session is a prerequisite; this example does not establish how easy that is.

affected_users.rationale: Assume one user's session is compromised and tenant isolation otherwise holds.

discoverability.rationale: An authenticated attacker could investigate session behavior; deployment details are unknown.

tests.text:
Scenario: Revoked session is rejected
  Given a revoked session belonging to a document owner
  When a document is requested with that session
  Then access is denied and no document content is returned

Scenario: Tenant boundary remains enforced
  Given an active session for a user in tenant A
  When a document in tenant B is requested
  Then access is denied without revealing document metadata
